newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures trade sideways, await API data.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures trade sideways, await API data.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures traded sideways after making early gains but the recovery from the heavy losses suffered in recent days was weak, traders said.
Activity was cautious ahead of tonight's release of U.S. inventory data which traders hoped would give the market some direction.
At 16.40 July Brent was trading at $17.69 a barrel, 13 cents up on Monday's close but little changed from midday. June gas oil was also slightly healthier, closing $1.50 up at $161.50 a tonne.
"It was fairly orderly today," said a trader.
"We saw some strength after New York opened but then that died away," said another broker.
Much of today's gas oil volume was on the spreads, with dealers rolling forward June positions, and some evidence of tightening on the June/July, players said.
"If (Brent and gas oil) manage to hold above the spring lows, we have a chance for a bounce," said Charles Gray of brokers Prudential Bache.
Prompt Brent futures shed 76 cents during trading on Friday and Monday, the latest in a string of falls that have knocked $3 off the price of a barrel in less than a month.

Rising U.S. crude and gasoline stocks gave investment funds an excuse to bale out of the market last Friday and this week's American Petroleum Institute (API) figures could again set short-term market direction.
Last week's API data showed crude stocks rose 8.44 million barrels while gasoline stocks were up by 261,000 barrels.

Data for the 15 European Union countries plus Norway released on Tuesday showed crude stocks fell 3.65 million barrels in May. Gasoline stocks were down 5.95 million barrels over the month, Stichting Euroilstock said.
